name: Mailgun
summary: Mailgun sends email through a REST API or SMTP. Paid plans start at $15 a month for 10,000 emails, and the free plan allows 100 emails a day. Log retention grows from 1 day on Free and Basic to 30 days on Scale, the only plan with SAML single sign-on.

facts.text: The events page says Mailgun retains event data for 30 days and that access varies by plan, while the pricing page lists log retention of 1 day on Free and Basic, 5 days on Foundation and 30 days on Scale.
Events cover delivered, failed and complained messages. A complaint is recorded when the recipient marks the email as spam and a feedback loop reports it.
Bounced addresses appear on the Suppressions tab, and Mailgun stops sending to addresses on its Do Not Send lists.
Mailgun states that it is SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001 certified and GDPR compliant.

plans.name: Free
plans.notes: 1 custom domain, 2 API keys, 1 user, 1 day of logs

plans.name: Basic
plans.notes: Extra emails from $1.80 per 1,000. 1 day of logs

plans.name: Foundation
plans.notes: First month free. Extra emails from $1.30 per 1,000. 5 days of logs

plans.name: Scale
plans.notes: First month free. Extra emails from $1.10 per 1,000. 30 days of logs and SAML single sign-on

hiddenCosts: A dedicated IP is listed as a $59 a month add-on per IP. The page is inconsistent about whether Foundation includes one, so ask before buying.
Email validation overages start at $1.20 per 100 validations on Basic and Foundation and $0.80 on Scale.
Dedicated IP pools, send time optimization and scheduled reports are limited to Scale.

contract.cancellation: The terms require a non-renewal notice at least 30 days before the current term ends. Either side can end the agreement for breach after a 45-day cure period.
contract.dataExport: The terms call customer data the customer's exclusive property and do not describe return or deletion after termination.
